title: Graph Powers — project configuration contract
description: What each repository declares in .graph-powers/config.json so the plugin can adapt to it. Every field has a safe default: a project without this file keeps working, just with the defaults. Point your config's $schema field here and your editor validates as you type. A project that only ever runs Claude Code may keep the file at .claude/config.json instead; both locations are read, .graph-powers/ first. The same file also works at ~/.graph-powers/config.json, where it states the operator's own posture for every repository they open; only the autonomy, graphGuardrails, protectedFiles and autoUpdate blocks are read from there, and a project's own file always outranks it.

project.description: Identity. Shows up in reports and gate messages; nothing here changes behaviour.

stack.description: Free-form stack identifier. Stack-gated skills and rules read this — 'astro' turns on the astro skill.

git.description: The git rails. Read by git_commit_gate, git_push_gate, git_branch_gate and branch_session_notice.

workBranch.description: The branch work happens on. A session that starts outside it gets a notice.

protectedBranches.description: No checkout that lands HEAD here, and no push, without an explicit opt-in in the turn.

optInPrefix.description: Prefix of the keys that release a risky action: <PREFIX>_ALLOW_COMMIT, _ALLOW_PUSH, _ALLOW_PUSH_MAIN, _ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT, _ALLOW_SPAWN_OVER, _ALLOW_OFF_LEASE. Use one prefix per project: with the same key in two repositories, an approval given in one starts counting in the other.

tooling.description: The commands the gates run. Without these, a gate 'passes' because the command does not exist.

linter.description: Name of the linter, for reporting only. It must be installed and on PATH for tooling.commands.lint to run; install it globally.

testRunner.description: null when the project has no tests — the case for static sites. Declaring null beats omitting it: it says the absence is deliberate.

commands.description: The literal command per gate. Whatever is here beats any inference.

lint.description: The tool itself must be installed and resolvable on PATH. This plugin runs the command you declare and nothing more: if it names biome, oxlint, eslint or prettier and that binary is absent, the run fails and the session is told at startup rather than silently skipping. Install globally (bun add -g @biomejs/biome oxlint, or npm i -g ...) so it works in every repository a session visits, not only one that carries it as a dependency. A command routed through the package manager (npm run lint) is not checked - the tool is named in the manifest, not here.

format.description: The tool itself must be installed and resolvable on PATH. This plugin runs the command you declare and nothing more: if it names biome, oxlint, eslint or prettier and that binary is absent, the run fails and the session is told at startup rather than silently skipping. Install globally (bun add -g @biomejs/biome oxlint, or npm i -g ...) so it works in every repository a session visits, not only one that carries it as a dependency. A command routed through the package manager (npm run lint) is not checked - the tool is named in the manifest, not here.

deadCode.description: A dead-code detector, run diff-scoped by the verify chain. Absent means the sweep is skipped, not faked.

renderHealth.description: An advisory render/effect health scan, run only under the verify chain's deep flag. Usually networked, which is why it is opt-in twice.

paths.description: Where the code lives. A single app sets frontendRoot='src' and omits the rest. An empty field means the project has no such layer — plans must not invent one.

mobileRoot.description: Where the mobile app lives. Absent removes mobile-developer from every routing enum: an agent with nothing to work on is worse than no agent.

database.description: Optional. Schema-state commands and the irreversible apply edge. Absent means the project has no database, or has not declared one — /verify reports NOT DECLARED when the schema surface moved, never PASS. The harness never branches on engine.

engine.description: Reporting only. The harness never branches on this value.

commands.description: The literal commands. status is read-only; generate writes the migration artefact in the repo; apply is the irreversible edge and /verify never runs it.

status.description: Read-only. Is the declared schema applied? Exit 0 means applied; non-zero is classified by output class, never by exit code alone.

generate.description: Writes the migration artefact in the repository. Does not touch the database.

apply.description: The irreversible edge. /verify never runs this. /implement runs it only when applyPolicy is optIn and the user approved this turn, then re-runs status.

applyPolicy.description: never: print the apply command and stop. optIn: /implement may run apply after explicit current-turn approval. /verify never applies under either value.

codex.description: Codex CLI specifics. Only read when generating .codex/ artefacts; ignored under Claude Code.

model.description: Model written into generated .codex/agents/*.toml. Left to the project because model names age faster than this plugin does.

reasoningEffort.description: model_reasoning_effort for generated subagents. The node that judges runs high — a cheap judge produces a false positive other nodes 'correct', and the origin of the error is lost.

skillsDir.description: Where the installer writes skills for Codex. Codex also reads ~/.agents/skills at user scope.

chain.description: What the plan/build/verify chain needs to know about THIS repository. The workflows ship the mechanism; every array here is the content, and it is the project's. A project that declares nothing still gets the full generic pass — these fields exist so that adopting the plugin never costs a repository review coverage it already had.

enabled.description: Whether /plan runs the full chain after the plan is approved. False stops at the plan file.

commitOnGreen.description: Commit automatically when verification returns VERIFIED. Off by default: a stranger's first session should not be the one that discovers the harness commits. Never pushes, and never fires on VERIFIED-WITH-NOTES or NEEDS-WORK.

maxFixRounds.description: Fix rounds before the verify chain stops and reports what is still open. Absent lets the workflow choose from its token budget.

riskSurfaces.description: The surfaces that floor a task at L4 and switch on the pre-mortem, the ADR and the architecture pass. Name yours if they differ; the default list is not universal.

hardRules.description: Non-negotiable conventions injected verbatim into every implementer prompt. One rule per line, phrased as an instruction.
examples: Use semantic design tokens only — never a color literal in a component.

invariants.description: Code that LOOKS redundant and must never be simplified away — a tenant filter, a PII gate, an idempotency guard. The simplify pass is told to report the skip instead of removing it. This is the field that prevents the most expensive class of automated cleanup damage.
examples: Never remove the tenant filter on a query, even when it looks unreachable.

domainSkills.description: Which skill an implementer loads for conventions, by the files it is touching. Knowledge only — a skill that dispatches agents must not be listed here, because the workflow is already the orchestration.

match.description: Glob or plain description of the files this applies to.

surfaces.description: Extra change surfaces, on top of the path roots the plugin derives. Each one becomes a boolean the contract gates and lenses below can be gated on, so an untouched surface spawns no work at all.

match.description: How to recognise it in the change set — a path prefix or a regex, described plainly.

contractGates.description: Commands to run only when a given surface changed, reported as their own gate entries. This is where a project keeps the checks it already had beyond type-check/lint/test.

when.description: Surface names. Empty or absent means always.

needsServer.description: A command that must be running first, and stopped afterwards.

runtime.description: When this gate must run under something other than the project's default runtime.

lenses.description: Extra adversarial review lenses, on top of correctness, security, performance and design. Each lens is a distinct QUESTION — identical skeptics agree with each other and miss the same things.

agent.description: Which subagent asks it. Defaults to evaluator.

when.description: Surface names. Empty or absent means always.

checks.description: What this lens looks for, one item per check.

graphGuardrails.description: Hard ceilings on the execution graph, enforced by graph_guardrails.py. They exist to catch runaway loops, not to squeeze normal work — calibrate by measuring, not by guessing.

maxSpawnsPerSession.description: Agent spawns inside spawnWindowMinutes. Counted from session start instead, this became a session-lifetime quota: a long session hit it on the first spawn of an unrelated later task and then refused every spawn for the rest of the day.

maxRoundsPerAgent.description: Re-spawning the same specialist many times is the signature of a loop that is not converging.

spawnWindowMinutes.description: The rolling window, in minutes, that maxSpawnsPerSession and maxRoundsPerAgent are counted over. A runaway fan-out is a burst; a working session that spans a day is not one.

maxParallelWave.description: Agents in one wave of the build chain, and fixes in one round of the verify chain. An oversized wave is split and logged, never truncated.

maxTasksPerPlan.description: Runaway backstop: a plan with more tasks than this throws instead of quietly implementing part of it.

maxRepatch.description: How many times the verify chain re-patches one failing item before reporting it blocked. Without it a single unfixable item consumes every round.

protectedFiles.description: Files no agent writes, under any circumstance. Each list extends the generic defaults; it never replaces them.

gates.description: Quality thresholds (Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals, bundle size) consumed by the performance skill, plus the audit this project wants run before a commit.

lighthouse.description: Minimum Lighthouse category scores, 0-100. A gate whose threshold is not written down is a gate that moves whenever the run is inconvenient.

preCommitAudit.description: A command run before `git commit` and `git push`. Exit 0 lets the commit proceed; anything else blocks it and shows the command's own output. Declare nothing and no audit runs — the plugin never picks a tool for the project, and never fetches one from the network on its own initiative. Released for one command with <PREFIX>_ALLOW_AUDIT=1.

timeout.description: Seconds. A slow audit on every commit is a hook people disable.

autonomy.description: How much the agent does without stopping to ask. This is the field that decides whether a session feels like work or like clicking Approve. Read by smart_bash_approver, tool_approver and the three git gates, and used by the installer to write a matching permissions allowlist. Also readable from ~/.graph-powers/config.json. A user-scope policy may always tighten; loosening routine Bash policy machine-wide requires machineWide=true, and never carries git auto or destructiveFloor=false across repositories. A project that declares its own autonomy block overrides the user's.

machineWide.description: User-scope opt-in only. In ~/.graph-powers/config.json, true allows level=autonomous (or bashDefault/cleanup=allow) to apply to repositories that declare no autonomy block. It never makes git auto and never disables the destructive floor. Without it, user scope may tighten policy but may not loosen it machine-wide. A project-scoped value has no effect.

level.description: guarded: an unrecognised command asks, and commit/push/protected-branch need an explicit opt-in key in the turn. autonomous: unrecognised commands run, cleanup runs, and the git gates pass without a key — the destructive floor below still holds. Everything under this group overrides the level individually, so 'autonomous but still ask before pushing' is one field, not a fork.

bashDefault.description: What happens to a command matching no known pattern. Defaults to ask under guarded and allow under autonomous. This single field is the source of most approval prompts.

cleanup.description: Deleting build output, caches, __pycache__, logs. Defaults to ask under guarded and allow under autonomous.

toolDefault.description: Every tool that is not Bash: subagent spawns, MCP calls, fetches, workflows, file tools. Defaults to ask under guarded and allow under autonomous. bashDefault only ever answered for shell commands, so a project on autonomous still stopped on tool calls git undoes for free; this is that same decision for the rest of the session. Read by tool_approver at PermissionRequest, which never answers for Bash and never reaches a call the PreToolUse floors already denied.

git.description: Per-action git autonomy. 'auto' means the gate passes without the opt-in key; the gate still runs and still reports what it let through.

protectedBranch.description: Checking out or pushing to a protected branch. Left at ask even under autonomous by default: it is the one git action whose blast radius is other people.

destructiveFloor.description: Keep refusing the operations git cannot undo, at any autonomy level: rm -rf on / or the home directory, mkfs, dd to a device, chmod -R 777 /, --no-preserve-root, DROP DATABASE, TRUNCATE, and force-pushing a protected branch. Deleting files inside a committed repository is not on this list — git restores those, so autonomous mode does it without asking. Set false to remove even this floor; nothing else in the harness will stop those commands.

allowPackageManagers.description: Package managers this project accepts. Empty or absent means all of them. Set it only when mixing managers actually breaks the project — a lockfile that must not fork.

autoUpdate.description: Whether the harness keeps itself at the published version. A plugin is a copy, and a copy starts ageing the moment it is installed — six months later five machines run five versions of guardrails that were meant to be identical. The check runs at session start, in a detached process, at most once per interval; it never delays the session and never touches anything inside the project.

enabled.description: false disables the check entirely. GRAPH_POWERS_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 does the same for one machine without editing the project's config.

intervalHours.description: Minimum hours between checks. The throttle is recorded before the check runs, so a failed check backs off instead of retrying every session.

claude.description: Update the Claude Code plugin (claude plugin marketplace update, then claude plugin update). The new version applies at the next session start, never mid-session.

codex.description: Regenerate the Codex artefacts when the registry version moved. Skipped when it did not: rewriting .codex/hooks.json costs a /hooks re-approval, and the guardrails stay inert until it is given.

grok.description: Update the Grok CLI plugin (grok plugin marketplace update, then grok plugin update). The new version applies at the next session start.
